div.div:
1 بَتَلَهُ , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor.
بَتِلَ , (S,) or
بَتُلَ , (Msb,) or both, (M, K,) inf. n. بَتْلٌ, (Lth, T, S, &c.,) He cut it off, or severed it; (M, Msb, K;) as also ↓ بتّلهُ , (M, K,) inf. n. تَبْتِيلٌ: (TA:) he separated it (Lth, T, S, M, Msb, K) from another thing. (Lth, T, S, M, K.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] بَتَلَ العُمْرَةَ He made the performance of the عمرة [or minor pilgrimage] to be obligatory, by itself. (A, TA.) And العُمْرَى ↓ بتّل He made the عمرى to be obligatory [upon himself]; i. e., the saying, I have assigned to thee my house that thou mayest inhabit it to the end of my life. (TA.) ＝
-A2- بَتِلَ, aor.
بَتَلَ , inf. n. بَتْلٌ, [but accord. to analogy, this should rather be بَتلٌ,] He (a man) was, or became, wide between the shoulders. (T.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
